points.title: 童年成长
points.description: 沃尔特·惠特曼于1819年5月31日出生在纽约州长岛的亨廷顿附近的一个农村家庭。他是九个孩子中的第二个，父母是沃尔特和路易莎·惠特曼。他的父亲是木匠和农民，家庭生活简朴。这段时期惠特曼接触了自然和普通劳动人民的生活，这些元素后来深刻影响了他诗歌的主题和风格。他几乎没有接受正规教育，主要依靠自学和阅读大量书籍，包括莎士比亚、荷马和但丁的作品。这段乡村生活经历为他后来的民主思想和对普通人的赞美奠定了基础。
points.descriptionEn: Walt Whitman was born on May 31, 1819, near Huntington on Long Island, New York, into a working-class family of nine children. His father was a carpenter and farmer, and the family lived a simple rural life. During this period, Whitman developed a deep connection with nature and ordinary working people, elements that profoundly influenced his poetic themes and style. He received little formal education, relying primarily on self-education and extensive reading of authors like Shakespeare, Homer, and Dante. This rural upbringing laid the foundation for his later democratic ideals and celebration of the common man.

points.title: 记者生涯
points.description: 1830年代，惠特曼全家搬到纽约布鲁克林，年轻的惠特曼开始接触印刷业，先后在多家印刷厂当学徒。1838年，他创办了《长岛人》周刊，这是他首次尝试编辑工作。1841年，他成为《纽约曙光》的编辑，随后在多家报纸工作，包括《布鲁克林鹰报》和《纽约每日论坛报》。作为记者，他广泛游历城市，接触各阶层人物，积累了丰富的社会观察。这一时期他开始尝试写作，发表了一些散文和小说，但尚未形成独特的诗歌风格。1848年，他短暂前往新奥尔良，担任《新月报》编辑，这段南方经历加深了他对美国多样性的认识。
points.descriptionEn: In the 1830s, Whitman's family moved to Brooklyn, New York, where the young Whitman entered the printing industry, working as an apprentice in various print shops. In 1838, he founded the Long Islander, his first attempt at editing. By 1841, he had become editor of the New York Aurora and subsequently worked for several newspapers including the Brooklyn Eagle and the New York Daily Tribune. As a journalist, he extensively traveled throughout the city, interacting with people from all walks of life, accumulating rich social observations. During this period, he began experimenting with writing, publishing essays and fiction, though he had not yet developed his distinctive poetic voice. In 1848, he briefly traveled to New Orleans to edit the Crescent City, a southern experience that deepened his understanding of American diversity.

points.title: 诗歌创作转型
points.description: 1850年代，惠特曼开始全身心投入诗歌创作，放弃了大部分新闻工作。他深受爱默生超验主义思想影响，开始探索一种全新的自由诗体。1855年，他自费出版了《草叶集》的第一版，包含12首诗，封面是他自己的肖像。这部作品彻底打破了传统诗歌的格律束缚，采用自由奔放的长句，赞美普通人和美国民主。惠特曼将诗集献给爱默生，后者回信称赞它是'美国迄今为止最才智横溢的才华展现'。这一时期的创作标志着惠特曼从记者到伟大诗人的转变，奠定了他在美国文学史上的独特地位。
points.descriptionEn: During the 1850s, Whitman devoted himself entirely to poetry writing, abandoning most of his journalistic work. He was deeply influenced by Emerson's transcendentalist philosophy and began exploring a revolutionary free verse style. In 1855, he self-published the first edition of Leaves of Grass, containing 12 poems with a portrait of himself on the cover. This work completely broke from traditional poetic constraints, employing free-flowing long lines to celebrate ordinary people and American democracy. Whitman dedicated the collection to Emerson, who replied with praise, calling it 'the most extraordinary piece of wit and wisdom that America has yet contributed.' This period marked Whitman's transformation from journalist to great poet, establishing his unique place in American literary history.

points.title: 诗人声名鹊起
points.description: 1856年至1862年间，惠特曼继续扩展《草叶集》，第二版增加到32首诗，包括后来著名的《我歌唱自己》和《一路摆过布鲁克林渡口》。他开始在文学圈获得认可，尽管同时也面临保守批评家的猛烈抨击，指责他的作品道德败坏、亵渎神明。惠特曼在这一时期还担任《布鲁克林时报》的编辑，同时继续创作诗歌。他的诗歌风格日益成熟，主题更加丰富，开始探索生与死、肉体与灵魂等哲学命题。这一时期，惠特曼与多位知识分子建立了友谊，包括布朗森·奥尔科特和亨利·戴维·梭罗，这些关系进一步丰富了他的思想世界。
points.descriptionEn: Between 1856 and 1862, Whitman continued to expand Leaves of Grass, with the second edition growing to 32 poems, including later famous works like 'Song of Myself' and 'Crossing Brooklyn Ferry.' He began gaining recognition in literary circles, though simultaneously facing fierce criticism from conservative reviewers who accused his work of immorality and blasphemy. During this period, Whitman also served as editor for the Brooklyn Times while continuing his poetic创作. His poetic style matured significantly, with themes becoming more diverse as he began exploring philosophical questions about life and death, body and soul. Whitman formed friendships with several intellectuals during this time, including Bronson Alcott and Henry David Thoreau, relationships that further enriched his intellectual world.

points.title: 内战时期
points.description: 1862年，惠特曼的兄弟乔治在南北战争中受伤，惠特曼前往华盛顿特区探望，从此开始了他在战区的志愿服务。他担任护士助手，照顾伤员，在军队医院工作。这段经历深刻影响了他，使他直面战争的残酷和生命的脆弱。他写下了著名的《鼓啊！鼓！》、《黎明的旗帜》等战争诗歌，以及后来收录在《桴鼓集》中的作品。1865年，林肯遇刺后，惠特曼写下了《啊，船长！我的船长！》和《当紫丁香最近在庭院中绽放时》等悼念诗篇，这些作品成为美国文学中最著名的悼念诗歌。战争期间，惠特曼也继续扩展《草叶集》，出版了包含大量战争诗歌的新版本。
points.descriptionEn: In 1862, Whitman's brother George was wounded during the Civil War, prompting Whitman to travel to Washington D.C. to visit him, beginning his volunteer service in war zones. He served as a nursing assistant, caring for wounded soldiers and working in army hospitals. This experience profoundly affected him, confronting him directly with the brutality of war and the fragility of life. He wrote famous war poems such as 'Beat! Beat! Drums!' and 'Flag of the Disseminator,' later collected in Drum-Taps. After Lincoln's assassination in 1865, Whitman composed 'O Captain! My Captain!' and 'When Lilacs Last in the Dooryard Bloom'd,' which became among the most famous elegies in American literature. During the war, Whitman continued to expand Leaves of Grass, publishing new editions that included numerous war poems.

points.title: 晚年创作
points.description: 1865年后，惠特曼大部分时间居住在新泽西州的卡姆登，尽管健康状况逐渐恶化（他可能在1850年代就已感染梅毒）。这一时期，他继续创作和修订《草叶集》，出版了多个版本，最终包含近400首诗歌。他获得了越来越多的认可，包括1873年获得的波士顿市民奖和1888年牛津大学授予的荣誉学位。惠特曼的晚年作品更加内省，探索死亡、不朽和精神超越等主题。他完成了《民主远景》等散文集，并整理出版了《草叶集》的'作者版'。1892年3月26日，惠特曼在卡姆登去世，被安葬在哈利卡姆公墓。他的葬礼规模盛大，数千人参加，标志着美国文学史上一个时代的结束。
points.descriptionEn: After 1865, Whitman lived mostly in Camden, New Jersey, though his health gradually deteriorated (he likely contracted syphilis in the 1850s). During this period, he continued writing and revising Leaves of Grass, publishing multiple editions that eventually contained nearly 400 poems. He received increasing recognition, including the Boston Citizen's Award in 1873 and an honorary degree from Oxford University in 1888. Whitman's later works became more introspective, exploring themes of death, immortality, and spiritual transcendence. He completed prose collections like Democratic Vistas and prepared an 'author's edition' of Leaves of Grass. On March 26, 1892, Whitman died in Camden and was buried in Harleigh Cemetery. His funeral was large and attended by thousands, marking the end of an era in American literary history.

supporter.zh: 惠特曼被誉为美国最伟大的诗人之一，他的《草叶集》开创了美国诗歌的新纪元。他打破了传统诗歌的束缚，创造了自由诗体，赞美普通人和美国民主精神。惠特曼的作品体现了美国精神的包容性和多样性，他对身体、性和自然的坦诚表达在当时具有革命性意义。他的诗歌超越了时代限制，影响了后来的垮掉派诗人、意象派和整个现代主义文学传统。惠特曼被视为美国民主的诗人先知，他的作品至今仍激励着追求自由和平等的读者。
supporter.en: Whitman is regarded as one of America's greatest poets, and Leaves of Grass开创了美国诗歌的新纪元。He broke free from traditional poetic constraints, creating free verse that celebrated ordinary people and American democratic spirit. Whitman's work embodied the inclusivity and diversity of the American spirit, and his candid expressions about body, sexuality, and nature were revolutionary for his time. His poetry transcended its era, influencing later Beat poets, Imagists, and the entire modernist literary tradition. Whitman is seen as a poetic prophet of American democracy, and his work continues to inspire readers seeking freedom and equality today.

critic.zh: 惠特曼的作品也面临诸多批评。他的诗歌被指责为道德败坏、亵渎神明，尤其是对性和身体的直白描写在当时引起强烈争议。批评者认为他的诗歌结构松散，缺乏艺术控制，过于自恋和自我膨胀。他的政治立场也受到质疑，早期对奴隶制的模糊态度和后来对安德鲁·约翰逊政府的支持使他受到一些进步主义者的批评。此外，惠特曼的个人生活，包括可能存在的同性恋倾向，也成为争议焦点。这些批评反映了惠特曼作品在19世纪社会环境中的挑战性，以及他作为先驱者所面临的阻力。
critic.en: Whitman's work has also faced significant criticism. His poetry was condemned as morally corrupt and blasphemous, particularly for its candid depictions of sexuality and the body. Critics argued his poems lacked artistic control with their loose structure, excessive narcissism, and self-aggrandizement. His political stances were also questioned, including his ambiguous early position on slavery and later support for Andrew Johnson's administration, which drew criticism from some progressives. Additionally, Whitman's personal life, including possible homosexual tendencies, became a point of controversy. These criticisms reflect the challenging nature of Whitman's work within 19th-century social contexts and the resistance faced by pioneers.

objective.zh: 在历史学界和流行文化中，惠特曼被定义为美国文学现代性的奠基人之一。他的诗歌超越了简单的文学分类，成为美国文化身份的核心象征。惠特曼的形象在流行文化中经常与自由、民主和个性解放联系在一起，他的诗句被引用于各种政治和文化场合。学术界将惠特曼置于美国超验主义和浪漫主义传统中，同时也认为他预示了现代主义的发展。他的作品被翻译成多种语言，影响遍及全球。惠特曼的生平和创作体现了19世纪美国社会的转型，从农业社会到工业民主，从欧洲文化依赖到美国文化自信的形成过程。
objective.en: In historical scholarship and popular culture, Whitman is defined as one of the founders of American literary modernity. His poetry transcends simple literary classification, becoming a core symbol of American cultural identity. Whitman's image in popular culture is frequently associated with freedom, democracy, and individual liberation, with his verses quoted in various political and cultural contexts. Academia places Whitman within the American transcendentalist and romantic traditions while also recognizing him as a precursor to modernism. His works have been translated into numerous languages, with influence worldwide. Whitman's life and work embody the transformation of 19th-century American society from agricultural to industrial democracy, and from European cultural dependence to the formation of American cultural confidence.

self.zh: 我赞美我自己，歌唱我自己，我所讲的一切，将对你们也一样适合，因为属于我的每一个原子，也同样属于你。
self.en: I celebrate myself, and sing myself, And what I assume you shall assume, For every atom belonging to me as good belongs to you.

others.zh: 惠特曼是美国迄今为止最才智横溢的才华展现。我发现它无与伦比，令人欣喜若狂。
others.en: The most extraordinary piece of wit and wisdom that America has yet contributed. I find it unparalleled, and I am very much delighted with it.
